correctness.rationale: The half-graph neighborhood equations reduce exactly to the recurrence \((x_{i+1},y_{i+1})=(x_i+y_i,-x_i)\) with boundaries \(x_1+y_1=0\) and \(x_n+y_n=0\). The recurrence has period six. For nonzero \(t=x_1\), the final boundary holds exactly when \(n\equiv1\pmod3\); summing the six-periodic pair contributions gives weight zero for \(n\equiv1\pmod6\) and \(-2t\) for \(n\equiv4\pmod6\). The recurrence also proves the converse and completeness. Exhaustive direct checks through \(n=6\) agree.

value.rationale: Half graphs are canonical twin-free chain graphs, so they are a natural exact family for a neighborhood-linear domination invariant. The theorem gives a complete function classification, not merely a scalar value: nonzero balanced functions occur exactly for \(n\equiv1\pmod3\), while positive maximum weight occurs only for \(n\equiv4\pmod6\). This cleanly separates graphs with only the zero function from \(d\)-balanced graphs possessing nonzero balanced functions and from genuinely non-\(d\)-balanced half graphs.
